note: DERIVE_FROM_BEHAVIOR v1: 27 exported pure functions (typed number / string / boolean params and result) from 24 permissive repos outside lm-corpus. Examples are the upstream function run on a fixed input grid (every 3rd row, at most 14, as the starting training slice), extended only by following PeaceAI's own derive_under_specified refusals the way an issue author would (each added row and the gate that asked for it is in addedForGates; Auditor #491 B1); held out: the rest of the grid plus every probe point (neighbour and far probes) not in the training rows; the prose is the function's leading doc comment only (empty for 13), never its body. PeaceAI derives the recorded expression from the training examples alone (the prose is recorded for review and never given to the engine); it is right on every held-out row, and each recorded expression was reviewed equal to the upstream body on its whole typed domain (template literal = concatenation; the ternary and comparisons as written). The evidence test re-derives each expression from the recorded examples and checks the pinned module text contains the upstream function; no third-party code is run by the test. Round 3 (Auditor #491: if / cap / range / square forms): 11 cap-form functions added, 8 from the M88-M99 miner clones and 3 from GitHub code search for clamp01 (microsoft/vscode, voxel51/fiftyone, jakearchibald/jakearchibald.com), each re-derived on the round-3 engine from its grid slice plus only the rows its refusals asked for, and right on every held-out integer from -1200 to 1200.

examples.prose: Construct the canonical rule_id for an anomaly finding. Mirrors Chi-3's catalog-key pattern (`{detector}__{classifier}`) so the auto-trigger ladder and the anomaly catalog stay aligned. /

Build a stable string key for a (detector, classifier) tuple. Used as the URL path segment for subscribe / unsubscribe routes and as the in-memory dispatcher registration key. The dispatcher's `registerDetector` keys by `detector.detectorId` alone; Chi-3 keeps things compatible by treating (detectorId, classifierId) as the OPERATOR-VISIBLE key but registering each tuple's factory output under its detectorId. A future dispatcher-side composite-key extension lights up multiple classifiers per detector; Chi-3 ships the URL surface ready for that without forcing it. /

examples.prose: A saved offset is safe to restore only if the current content is at least tall enough to reach it. Content height (not max-scroll = content − viewport) is a deliberately generous bound: an offset that sits within the content but past the last viewport clamps harmlessly to the bottom (still valid rows), whereas an offset BEYOND the content — the shrunk-list case — is the only one that strands every row above the viewport. So that is the single case we reject; everything else restores as before.
